caption:
Two astronauts just gave the International Space Station a major power upgrade, and it took more than seven hours outside.

NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk completed a 7-hour, 11-minute spacewalk to install a new ISS Roll-Out Solar Array, or IROSA, on the station's 2A power channel. Menon rode the Canadarm2 robotic arm about 260 miles above Earth to start the installation. It was Menon's fourth spacewalk and Kutryk's first.

This is the seventh of eight new arrays. The astronauts also did prep work for another spacewalk on Thursday, Nov. 5, when the eighth and final array will go on the 3B power channel.

Once that is done, the eight new arrays will raise the station's electricity generation from 160 kilowatts to roughly 215 kilowatts, as much as 30% more. NASA says the extra power supports essential operations and the station's eventual safe, controlled deorbit.

The spacewalk was designated U.S. spacewalk 100 and was the 285th spacewalk for station assembly, maintenance and upgrades. Nearly three decades in, the station is still being rebuilt while people live on it.
